_comments._: Keys starting with _ are stripped by scripts/sync-vapi.ts. ${VAR} placeholders are filled at sync time; {{...}} / {% %} are Vapi Liquid.
_comments.model: gpt-4.1, temperature 0.5 (Vapi's default) for a warmer, less repetitive delivery; tool-call accuracy comes from the backend rules, not low temperature. FASTER ALTERNATIVE (not switched): "gpt-4.1-mini" (or the pinned "gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14") cuts model time per turn noticeably, but it's weaker at multi-step tool use and long instruction lists; this prompt has ~20 rules the backend can't enforce (call order, read-back, no invented facts). Switch only after `npm run evals -- --confirm` passes on it. Prompt caching: OpenAI caches identical prompt prefixes automatically, so the system prompt keeps the per-call date line at the END. promptCacheRetention '24h' (spec: supported on gpt-4.1 and GPT-5 models): calls are minutes or hours apart, longer than the default in-memory cache lives, so without it the ~4,300-token prompt is usually re-read cold.
_comments.transcriber: Deepgram Flux (flux-general-en): transcription and end-of-turn detection in one model. Measured on the Oct 21 calls with nova-3: endpointing p50 727 ms / p95 2250 ms (LiveKit 'Conservative' floor of 700 ms plus a 1.5 s rule) and transcriber p95 2.7 s (max 5 s). Flux decides end of turn from audio and text together (Deepgram quotes ~260 ms EOT p50). eotThreshold 0.7 is Deepgram's default and its 'low-latency mode' value (0.5-0.6 is 'aggressive' and risks cut-ins); eotTimeoutMs 3000 is in the docs' 'fast' band (2000-3000): a turn ends 3 s after speech even if the model is unsure. Vapi docs: do NOT set smartEndpointingPlan with Flux, custom endpointing rules aren't evaluated, and transcriptionEndpointingPlan is ignored, so all three were removed (_removedFromLive tells vapi:sync to report them if the live assistant still has them). keyterm: 48 terms (Deepgram advises 20-50; 500-token cap). Deepgram supports keyterm on Flux; Vapi doesn't document forwarding it to Flux, so check a transcript for brand and street names after the first call. Fallback: --variant gpt-4.1-nova3 (nova-3 + LiveKit 'Normal' curve).
_comments.voice: Provider and voiceId are a placeholder until the owner picks one (see README 'Voice options'). chunkPlan: TTS gets whole sentences (no comma boundaries, so speech isn't choppy), but minCharacters is 5 (Vapi default 30): a short opener like "Got it." is sent to the voice on its own, so audio starts while the model is still writing the rest. Measured voice latency is ~230 ms either way; this removes the wait for a 30-character first chunk. formatPlan.replacements respell names the TTS mispronounced before synthesis: live transcripts heard the greeting's 'Ava' as 'Eva', so it's spelled 'Ayva' (AY-vuh). A Vapi pronunciation dictionary isn't used: on version-2 Vapi voices it reroutes the voice through Cartesia, which would change the voice. Replacements need chunkPlan.enabled; they may not apply to firstMessage (undocumented), so firstMessage spells 'Ayva' itself.
_comments.startSpeakingPlan: waitSeconds 0.3: the low end of Vapi's customer-service range (0.3-0.5; 0-0.2 is for 'gaming, real-time'). Endpointing itself is Flux's job (see transcriber). If test calls show no cut-ins, 0.2 is the next step.
_comments.stopSpeakingPlan: numWords 2: 'uh-huh' doesn't interrupt Ava; a real interruption of 2+ words does. acknowledgementPhrases per Vapi's Flux example: these never interrupt. backoffSeconds 1 before Ava resumes after being interrupted.
_comments.analysisPlan: Deprecated in the API but still works; feeds message.analysis.summary into our calls table. Migrate to structured outputs later.
_comments.firstMessage: Never personalized: callers aren't verified at greeting time. assistant-request (ASSISTANT_REQUEST_ENABLED) only sets caller_recognized, used by the prompt. Vapi has no first-message delay for inbound calls (checked Oct 2026), so the opening words 'Hi, thanks for calling' are deliberately skippable if the line clips them.
_comments.firstMessageInterruptionsEnabled: false (Vapi's default): the caller's 'hello?' while the line connects doesn't cut the greeting off.
_comments.serverMessages: status-update: keep-warm (a non-blocking select 1 on 'in-progress'). phone-call-control: Vapi delegates hang-up and forwarding to /api/vapi/events, which waits HANGUP_TAIL_MS (1.5 s) and then ends the call via monitor.controlUrl. That's the goodbye tail padding for EVERY ending path (src/server/vapi/call-control.ts). monitorPlan.controlEnabled must stay true for that URL to exist.
_comments.endCall: Call endings (live: the model said its own goodbye, then Vapi's was cut off at 'Take', and Ava re-engaged after goodbye). Per docs.vapi.ai/tools/hang-up: when the endCall tool has a request-start message, Vapi speaks it instead of endCallMessage, then hangs up; the prompt tells the model never to say goodbye itself, only to call endCall. blocking:true makes the hang-up wait until the message is spoken. Belt and braces: the closing line ends with the endCallPhrases entry 'goodbye for now', and the docs say Vapi waits for the assistant to finish speaking before an end-call phrase hangs up. The phrase must never appear elsewhere (endCallPhrases match any assistant speech, e.g. the greeting). endCallMessage is the same line, used only if the tool's message is ever removed. Oct 21 measurement: the hang-up still landed 0.15-0.67 s before the goodbye audio ended, and the carrier dropped the tail on the phone (the recording was complete). Fixed with phone-call-control tail padding (see serverMessages).
_comments.backgroundSound: 'off' | 'office' | an audio URL. Vapi's default for phone calls is 'office' (ambient office noise), so it's set explicitly; 'off' by default.
_comments.hooks: Idle messages via customer.speech.timeout hooks, for silence mid-call (replaces the older messagePlan.idleMessages). They never fire after the call has ended.

name: Summit Air Virtual Assistant
firstMessage: Hi, thanks for calling Summit Air! This is Ayva, the virtual assistant. What's going on today?

messages.content: Thanks for calling Summit Air. Take care, and goodbye for now.

exact: I'm still here whenever you're ready.

messages.content: Summarize this Summit Air HVAC call for the office in 2-3 sentences: who called, the problem, urgency, and the outcome (booked window, priority dispatch, callback, safety stop, or nothing). Note anything the office must follow up on.
